title: TCP: Duplicate ACKs hidden by Window Update and SACK presence
description:
TCP: Duplicate ACKs hidden by Window Update and SACK presence
    
Duplicate ACKs are not always well identified particularly when
the client is answering with SACK information and a Window Update,
leading to a wrong analysis of both client Duplicate ACKs and
sender Retransmissions instead of Fast Retransmissions.
  
Closes #14937.

If this is "a Dup ACK _rather_ than a Window Update", should we be clearing the WINDOW_UPDATE flag instead of just adding the DUP flag? The discussion in #14937 seems to lean towards that.

If we do so, we wouldn't have to change the colorfilters files.

The User Guide is indeed somewhat saying these flags are mutually exclusive 
> (TCP Dup ACK : The window size is non-zero and hasn’t changed.)

However that was of course not written for this particular case #14937 , but it makes more sense to keep the original idea and extend it by loosening "hasn't changed" criteria. At the end : if the _Window_ changes, it's not a _Dup ACK_, unless it's a _SACK_, and the User Guide also needs a couple of words more.

I will update shortly.
With the latest commit : WINDOW_UPDATE cleared, colorfilter restored, doc updated.

 Set when all of the following are true:
 
 * The segment size is zero.
-* The window size is non-zero and hasn’t changed.
+* The window size is non-zero and hasn’t changed, or there is valid SACK data.
 * The next expected sequence number and last-seen acknowledgment number are non-zero (i.e., the connection has been established).
 * SYN, FIN, and RST are not set.
 
@@ -644,7 +644,7 @@ reverse direction.
 Set when the all of the following are true:
 
 * The segment size is zero.
-* The window size is non-zero and not equal to the last-seen window size.
+* The window size is non-zero and not equal to the last-seen window size, and there is no valid SACK data.
 * The sequence number is equal to the next expected sequence number.
 * The acknowledgment number is equal to the last-seen acknowledgment number,
 * or to the next expected sequence number when answering to a ZeroWindowProbe.
